summary_paragraph: A woman with history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass status post reversal complicated by chronic abdominal pain, bacterial overgrowth, hypoglycemia requiring tube feeds, and prior ulcer disease was admitted three days after a prior discharge with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain now localized around the gastrostomy tube site. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, a benign abdominal exam without peritoneal signs, no clear evidence of G-tube site infection, and abdominal radiographs with a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern and no free air, with gaseous stomach distention possibly contributing. Tube feeds were held overnight and then restarted at goal without worsening pain; home GI medications and antibiotics were continued, and gabapentin was increased to 600 mg three times daily for suspected abdominal wall pain (supported by a positive Carnett’s sign). She met with social work for coping and care-planning, and was discharged home ambulatory at her baseline pain level, tolerating clears by mouth and tube feeds, with outpatient GI follow-up guidance and a plan for repeat CBC in one week for mild leukopenia noted during admission.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
